title: The Dock Foreman's Crates
story:
The morning sun came up bright over the riverfront of San Antonio del Río, filling the docks with the rumble of motorized river launches and the heavy thud of wooden crates. James sat on a stack of dry cedar planks, watching dockworkers load cargo along the wooden quays. Near the main gangway, a dock foreman in thick work clothes winced as he picked up a rough pine crate, rubbing his palms where sharp wooden splinters dug into his hands.

Having spent days learning to sand wood with Don Tadeo back in Aldea San Gabriel, James recognized the unplaned timber right away. He reached down for the small brass magnifying lens hanging around his neck on its green ribbon. Stepping carefully onto the dock boards, James held the glass over the wooden crate handle, using the sunlight to pinpoint a cluster of tiny, hidden splinters wedged deep in the grain.

The foreman paused, chuckling softly in surprise as the small monkey pointed out the sharp burrs before the heavy loads were lifted. Nico watched wide-eyed from the top of a salt barrel as James moved along the row of crates, using his lens to inspect handle after handle and tapping the rough spots so the workers could file them smooth. The task was steady and rhythmic, blending easily into the lively bustle of the wharf.

By midday, the foreman handed James two sweet yellow plums and a warm corn tamal wrapped in a banana leaf. James and Nico sat together on a shaded bench by the river landing to eat, enjoying the steaming corn and sweet fruit as cargo boats hummed past on the water.
location: Riverside docks of San Antonio del Río
